interpret.prompt:
You are labeling a short first-person video clip (about half a second) recorded by an agent moving on the
inside surface of a colorful torus world. The surface is painted with bands of color around a wheel:
cyan, blue, purple, pink, red, orange, yellow, light green, green. The frames may be LOW-RESOLUTION or BLURRY —
judge the dominant HUE, not fine texture. Report the color of the surface the agent is STANDING ON: look ONLY at
the immediate foreground floor at the BOTTOM-CENTER of the frame (ignore the walls, the far distance, and any
colors elsewhere in the view). Choose the single closest match from the listed colors; if it is between two,
pick the more dominant / more saturated one. In "reasoning", FIRST briefly describe what you see on the
bottom-center floor (a few words), THEN commit to the color. Also give a self_reported_confidence in [0,1]
(lower it when the frames are blurry or ambiguous). Return ONLY the structured fields.
interpret.caption_prompt:
ALSO write exactly {n} short, natural-language captions, each describing THIS specific clip in a DIFFERENT
way, as if telling someone what the agent is seeing and doing. Take into account the color of the surface it
is standing on and where it sits on the ring vertically (near the top, around the middle, or near the bottom),
and mention any motion you can see (climbing, descending, drifting left or right, fast or slow). Vary the
wording, word order, and level of detail across the {n} captions — some terse ("red floor, near the top"),
some fuller ("moving along a bright red band high up on the ring, drifting to the left"). Do NOT number them
or reuse a fixed template; make them read like distinct human descriptions of the same moment. If any "Known
exact facts" are given (e.g. the vertical position on the ring), treat them as ground truth and make EVERY
caption consistent with them — the frames can be misleading about position, so trust the stated facts there.

run_summary.problem: block-stack is a brand new 2.06 hour xArm7 teleop corpus and no world model has been trained on it. At its native 30 Hz the per-step image change on scene_right is 0.0193 RMSE which is only 0.30x a robocasa-like codec error floor of 0.0637 -- below the floor where record 13 showed that predicting zero motion is the correct solution to the objective.
run_summary.tried: On robocasa every early run at 20 Hz sat at 0.61x the floor and hedged to zero motion. More action gradient (5.8x to 16x) changed nothing and Fourier action features changed nothing. Subsampling to 4-5 Hz was the fix there and every published robot world model that controls long rollouts subsamples to 2-5 Hz.
run_summary.trying: Transplant the robocasa record-holding two-camera recipe onto block-stack and vary ONLY the temporal stride to find the operating point on this data.
run_summary.trying_detail: subsample 10 gives 3 Hz. scene_right sits at 1.03x to 1.46x the floor depending on where the true floor lands and gripper_right_top at 1.73x to 2.44x. F=64 spans 24.0 s of real time and 84 percent of stride-1 training windows survive. Relaunched once at the start because the first attempt had no WANDB_API_KEY in its environment and was logging locally only. Relaunched a second time because check_val_every_n_epoch=2 sets the VAL cadence only and the eval suite was still on its default every_epochs=10 plus at_epochs 5 and 15 so ae_floor would not have run until epoch 5. Relaunched a third time after merging main, which added data.action_aggregate: the default sum was scaling the action input by the stride because these are autocorrelated stick positions not deltas, giving 30 to 45 sigma excursions and a 1.5x action-scale difference between the two arms. Now mean.
run_summary.rationale: Any camera or loss comparison run below the codec floor returns a null result that means nothing. Fix the rate first then use the winner as the platform for the four-camera question. Strides 10 and 15 are the pair that stay at or above 1.0x across the whole plausible floor range 0.045 to 0.0637 -- stride 6 would be 0.82x to 0.92x if the floor is robocasa-like. The error is asymmetric because below the floor is degenerate while above it is merely harder.
